description.p: Radix is a desktop calculator with a history-centric workflow: every evaluated equation becomes a history row whose results re-render live when the number format, grouping or number base changes.

It offers Basic, Advanced, Financial, Programming, Keyboard and Conversion modes; arbitrary-precision arithmetic with exact rational results; trigonometry with configurable angle units; bitwise operations with a selectable word size; live unit and currency conversion; and four result formats (Automatic, Fixed, Scientific, Engineering).
Documentation release: adds doc 17, a black-box audit of mode-switch animations, together with its capture scripts and evidence, and updates the documentation index and coverage report.
Third release candidate: the Basic keypad now has square (^) and square root (√) keys, the parser reports UTF-8 byte spans, and a number next to a prefix square root multiplies implicitly (5√5).

Second release candidate: the random bit flip preference now has a configurable "Bit Flip Frequency" (0-100%, default 12%), and the application icon is the owner-provided calculator-tile artwork with freshly rendered hicolor sizes.

First release candidate of the 51.0.0 series, tracking GNOME Calculator 51. The deliberate arithmetic corrections (2+2=5, 1+1=3, 9+10=21 and division by zero = 67) are now behind an opt-in "Apply 2026 math fixes" preference, off by default.
A separate "Apply random bit flips" preference can flip a bit of the expression before evaluation using /dev/urandom. Both settings are saved between sessions.
Initial independent implementation of the Radix behavioral specification.
